column1: # Live RBAC route matrix: Phase 1 (hardening). Each step adds the rows of the behaviour it
# changes; a baseline row whose answer a step changes is tagged superseded-by:p1 there.
# Columns: id, since, actor, method, path, body, expect, tags (see tests/rbac_matrix_live.sh).
# ---- step 1.1: role and existence come from the database, not the 7-day login JWT ----
# rbac-admin-b signs in (and acts as member_a) while an admin and keeps those cookies; the
# runner demotes it to standard by SQL just before each *_demoted row and restores it right
# after. Each control sends the same request as the admin. POST /api/users gets a body it
# refuses after its admin check (400), so no account is ever created.
# the act-as cookie minted while an admin stops counting once the account is demoted
# rbac-deleted signs in, is deleted by SQL, and its still-valid cookie is replayed: three
# former login-only routes, the current-account route, then a sign-in proving it is gone.
# ---- step 1.2: one password floor, email case ----
# A new password under 12 characters is refused with its code, so nothing is created or
# Emails are stored lowercase: an edit to an address another account holds in other
# capitals is refused, and sign-in finds the account whatever the case typed.
# ---- step 1.4: admin-on-admin actions need the acting admin's own password ----
# Every refused row lacks that password (or sends a wrong one), so nothing changes. The one
# wrong password counts one attempt against rbac-admin-a's step-up budget; the act-as row
# after it gives the right one and clears it (rows never keep a Set-Cookie, so the actor
# stays rbac-admin-a). The last-admin guard cannot answer 409 on a stack whose real admins
# remain: its race is proved on the locked transaction itself (route.concurrentDemote.test.ts).
# a member target needs no step-up; a demotion runs in the locked transaction even when the
# account is already standard, so this proves the advisory lock on the deployed build
# ---- step 1.6: the admin bypass is a masked read; a re-pointed endpoint needs its secret again ----
# Every refused row is refused at the gate, before anything is written or sent. The managed and
# owner controls send a body their handler refuses after the gate (chat-skills POST {} -> 400
# "name is required"), so nothing is created there either.
# act-as a member who can sign in grants no write either
# the read stays, masked: the seeded fake bearer never comes back
# revoking another account's token stays an admin action: the gate admits it (no such token: 404)
# a passwordless managed account is written through act-as, and only through it
# the owner re-pointing a saved MCP server (save or test) with the masked token is refused
# ---- step 1.14: a ticket names its socket; the Kali terminal needs the terminal grant ----
# A member seeded after the upgrade holds no legacy grant (the backfill's cutoff came first), so
# its terminal ticket is refused and its chat and CypherFix tickets are not. An admin opens the
# terminal through its own role, also while acting as the member. An allowed mint writes nothing
# but, for the terminal, an agent.terminal_opened row the cleanup removes. The legacy holder and
# The unmasked tunnel credentials answer only the internal key (HD-05): every session, an
# admin's included, gets 404 (anonymous keeps the middleware's 401, baseline). Changing the
# tunnel takes an admin, the member holding the `tunnels` legacy grant or a pre-upgrade account
# under the escape hatch (HD-06); the seeded members hold no grant (the legacy holder:
# tests/test_e2e_security_live.sh and testing/e2e/tests/rbacTunnels.spec.ts). Rows that pass
# the tunnel check send a GitHub Enterprise host the route refuses after it (400), so nothing
# is written or pushed to the sandbox; refused rows stop at the tunnel check. The settings GET
# tells the page whether to offer the controls. With the identity switch on these settings are
# instance settings (step 2.4): the rows tagged identity:off have identity:on twins in p2.tsv.
# The settings row also carries the MCP servers JSON: the admin's masked read of /settings
# returns the seeded server with its bearer masked (the /mcp read is p1-admin-reads-other-masked).
# Re-pointing a saved MCP server with a NEW token typed passes the re-entry rule but asks for the
# signed-in user's password (ID-25): refused before anything is written, the stored bearer never
# answered. (A wrong password would count toward member_a's step-up lockout, so no row sends one.)
# Refusals only, so nothing is written: the allowed selection row is refused afterwards by
# the numeric bounds (nucleiRateLimit 0), which run after the template check. The uploads,
# the overwrite, the promotion, a scan's filtered read and the user-delete handover need
# multipart bodies and SQL: tests/rbac_nuclei_templates_live.sh. aem-json-exposure.yaml
# ships in mcp/nuclei-templates, so it is an instance template (the upgrade backfill).
# GET tells the toolbar whose agent runs a press stops (HD-07): every user's for an admin
# (also while acting as a member), the member's own otherwise. A member's POST stops only
# that member's runs: member_c has none, so it stops nothing and no one else's. No row POSTs
# as an admin, the instance-wide stop, which would end other people's runs on a shared stack;
# the stop itself is checked live with two members' stub-model runs, one stopped, one not.
# ---- step 1.9: the agent's webapp-only routes, MCP reload / manifest / test, stdio servers ----
# A member's stdio server or draft is refused before anything is written or spawned (NF-14,
# audited), and so is a server naming an agent variable as its bearer (OQ-R1). The admin's
# stdio save is refused AFTER the stdio check by the schema (no name), so nothing is written.
# No row reloads the shared agent as an admin (it would reconnect every user's MCP tools).
# includeSkillContent answers the master key only (NF-15): the owner's browser and an admin
# acting as the owner get the project without the raw servers.
# The live stack holds no Metasploit session to show (a real one is manual checkpoint M4;
# run_artifacts/step113/drive.mjs proves the per-project view with a tagged listener), so
# these rows prove the gate on ids outside the caller's view: such an id is 404 before any
# command reaches the console (the baseline's 422 was the agent refusing a non-numeric id).
# member_c owns nothing and holds no grant, so its list never carries a job. A 502
# session_manager_unauthorized means the agent's MCP_AUTH_TOKEN differs from kali-sandbox's.
# ---- step 1.16: job credentials for scan containers ----
# The bare scanner key reads and writes nothing (HD-20): each scanner route wants the scan's job
# credential beside it, which the matrix cannot send (tests/rbac_job_credential_live.sh mints
# one inside the agent container and proves the reads it opens). The master key is unchanged.
# ---- step 1.18: the legacy access review, the update notes and the admins' rbac block ----
# Reads and refusals only: no row decides a grant, since that would decide this stack's real
# members' grants; tests/rbac_legacy_review_live.sh makes fixture-only decisions.
# ---- step 1.20: the last baseline hole rows ----
# A member may upload and delete its own templates (F-07), so the baseline's two invalid-body
# probes still reach the body checks and keep their 400; the owner rules are the p1-nuclei-*
# rows above and tests/rbac_nuclei_templates_live.sh. The member's session list keeps its 200
# with its own projects' sessions only (p1-sessions-list-member), its template list its 200
# with its own and the instance templates (p1-nuclei-list-member).
